author: TEDx Talks
description: At 28, Tricia Rose Burt said no to a free demo reel from one of New York's biggest radio stations — and spent the next three decades wondering what would have happened if she'd said yes. In this talk, the storyteller and award-winning podcast host explores what it cost her to play it safe — and the audacious move she finally made to set things right. Tricia Rose Burt is an acclaimed storyteller and host of the award-winning podcast No Time To Be Timid, now in its fifth season. She spent her early career in public relations before leaving at 34 to cash out her retirement savings, move to Ireland, and become an artist. In her 40s she wrote and performed a one-woman show; in her 50s she stepped onto the stage with The Moth. Her work — across writing, performance, and audio — explores what we lose when we stay safe, and what becomes possible when we finally don't. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn mo
title: How I redeemed 35 years of regret | Tricia Rose Burt | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when a creative mind becomes so “turned on and tuned in” that the boundary between coincidence and cosmic meaning dissolves? In Chaos Under Glass, artist and educator Keith Wasserman shares the story of his first manic break during the Blizzard of 1996—and the decades-long journey to accept, align, and collaborate with his bipolar brain through art, mindfulness, and self-awareness. It is a moving exploration of creativity, mental health, synchronicity, and the healing power of artistic practice.
 Keith Wasserman is a multi-disciplined artist, musician, filmmaker, and creative facilitator whose work explores symbolism, synchronicity, mindfulness, and the beautifully chaotic nature of the human mind. Blending vulnerability with humor and philosophy with absurdity, he creates work that invites deeper reflection and authentic connection. Through art, public speaking, and community engagement, Wasserman encourages people to cultivate a healthier relationship with creativity, c
title: Framing a manic mind | Keith Wasserman | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When he was trapped in war-torn Mogadishu, Abdi Nor Iftin hid beneath his bed with a small tape recorder, secretly documenting his life amid fear and chaos. In this deeply personal TEDx talk, he reveals how storytelling became his lifeline — and how even the quietest voice can break through fear, censorship, and silence.
 Abdi Nor Iftin's story was featured on the acclaimed This American Life episode “Abdi and the Golden Ticket.” Today, he is a writer, speaker, and advocate for free expression, immigration, and human connection across cultures. Through his work, Abdi explores what it means to belong, to speak freely, and to hold onto hope in the darkest moments. In this talk, he shares the hidden recordings and experiences that helped him survive Mogadishu — and ultimately led him to find his voice in America. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Reporting from the most dangerous place on earth | Abdi Nor Iftin | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Millions of caregivers are holding families and the healthcare system together — without access to support, resources, or a billable diagnosis code. Most become caregivers following a life-changing health event, and are expected to manage complex care with little training or help. In this innovative and surprisingly funny talk, Cheryl Field, registered nurse, makes the case that caregiving should be recognized as a primary condition the healthcare system can no longer afford to ignore.
 Cheryl Field is a nurse, speaker, and three-time international best-selling author who helps families make sense of a system that often feels impossible to navigate. She shares practical guidance for caregivers online as Advocate Nurse Cheryl. With more than 30 years of experience spanning clinical care, healthcare leadership, quality, compliance, and reimbursement, she brings both bedside credibility and big-picture insight to one of the most urgent issues in healthcare today. Cheryl is the author of
title: The missing diagnosis in healthcare | Cheryl Elizabeth Field | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if beauty isn't just a frivolous luxury, but infrastructure for emotional well-being? For TEDx speaker Bridget Shannon, planting a few flowers was an attempt to feel grounded during the uncertainty of 2020. In her talk she shares how this simple practice unexpectedly transformed her mental health, and explores why tending beauty can restore hope, resilience, and a sense of purpose.
 Bridget Shannon is the owner of Nowadays Flowers, a cut flower farm and floral design studio cultivating joy, beauty, and connection. The Nowadays team creates garden-inspired weddings and events across New England, pops up around town with Clover the delightful vintage flower truck, and leads educational workshops. Bridget is a former Intuitive Eating Counselor and is certified in therapeutic horticulture. Through their Flourish program, Nowadays supports mental health and emotional well-being through flowers. What began as planting a few dahlias during the pandemic has grown into a mission centered
title: A flower farmer's case for tending beauty  | Bridget Shannon | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
After losing the woman she built her life with, cybersecurity architect Kate Scarcella found herself applying the same principles she used to restore compromised systems. In this deeply personal talk, she explores how grief, loss, and life-changing disruption require something surprisingly similar to system recovery: discovering what still works, what remains true, and what can respond.
 Kate Scarcella has spent more than 25 years helping organizations recover from some of their most challenging technology failures. A cybersecurity architect, advisor, and speaker, she has worked with Fortune 50 enterprises, served on IBM's Security Board of Advisors, and chairs the CI/CD Cybersecurity SIG at the Continuous Delivery Foundation. After the loss of her partner Jill following more than 35 years together, Kate discovered that the principles she used to restore compromised systems offered an unexpected framework for navigating grief and profound change. Her work explores what technology can
title: I lost my wife, then used cybersecurity to restore myself | Kate Scarcella | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In the dark Arctic winter, a strange clicking moves across the tundra — not branches, but reindeer tendons slipping over bone, an adaptation that helps them stay connected when vision fails. Scientist Michael Palace spent more than a decade there mapping change. He didn't expect that the reindeer — and the Sámi who herd them — would retrain how he listens, and how he does science. Michael Palace is an environmental scientist and professor at the University of New Hampshire whose research combines remote sensing, drones, field ecology, and geospatial science to study environmental change across Arctic, tropical, and temperate ecosystems. His work has been supported by NASA, NSF, USDA, USAID, USGS, DOD, and DOE. He is also an electronic musician and field recordist whose creative work explores the intersection of sound, technology, and the environment. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at http
title: Listening to reindeer in the dark | Michael Palace | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Is artificial intelligence everywhere, or is it only everywhere for the people who need it the least? In this talk, technologist Cameron Miner shares a vision for maximizing the impact of AI for all of humanity, exploring how frameworks like Digital Twins and modular, clean-energy data centers could bring intelligence to the communities and places that need it most. It's time to choose outcomes over income.
 Cameron Miner is charting a path to preserve human agency in the Age of AI. A parallel entrepreneur and 30-year technology veteran, his track record includes working on the SRI research team whose DARPA-funded work became the da Vinci surgical robot, pioneering wearables at IBM Research, developing the strategic research framework for neural-input AR wristbands at Meta (and earning a patent in the process), and founding the Digital Twin Working Group at MIT Lincoln Laboratory. He currently serves as Head of Innovation at Frontier Industries, where modular AI data centers and nucle
title: AI’s looming geography problem | Cameron Miner | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Scientific progress depends on imagining what might be true based on what we know right now, and then testing it. That's why scientific advice can change, and why science students need to learn to think creatively, not just memorize what's already been discovered. In this talk, Jessica Bolker reveals what Darwin's missing links have to do with peptic ulcers, changing Covid guidelines, and the need for creative writing projects in science classes.
 Professor Bolker is an evolutionary and developmental biologist who got distracted by philosophy. Educated at Yale, UC Berkeley, and Oxford, she is an award-winning faculty member at the University of New Hampshire and the originator of the Fictional Species Project as a core assignment for evolution students. Whether you think science is fascinating, boring, or too hard, this talk is for you. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.co
title: What Darwin and Covid have in common | Jessica Bolker | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
“I'll do it.” Those three words changed Shawn Walsh's life forever. Most people remember 9/11. Few talk about 9/12. After surviving the Pentagon attack, Walsh found himself responsible for helping recover and account for the dead. In this unforgettable TEDx talk, he reveals how responsibility arrives before we feel ready for it, and how the moments we never choose ultimately define who we become.

 Shawn Walsh is an author, strategist, and retired U.S. Army Colonel whose work in logistics, energy, and sustainment helped shape U.S. and allied military doctrine. During more than 25 years of military service, he held command and staff assignments worldwide, including Bosnia, Iraq, Germany, Korea, and the Pentagon. Following his Army career, he led initiatives focused on strengthening energy resilience and modernizing critical federal infrastructure. A graduate of The Citadel and the United States Army War College, Walsh is a Bronze Star recipient with more than four decades of leadership
title: Inside the Pentagon on 9/12  | Shawn Walsh | TEDxPortsmouth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this heartfelt and practical TEDx talk, Dr. Paula C. Perez challenges the myths that keep so many women waiting, wondering, and settling in their search for love. Drawing from her extraordinary personal journey from being a 49-year-old virgin to becoming a happily married preacher's wife, Dr. Perez shares the four essential steps that transformed not only her relationship status but her relationship with herself. Award-winning author, certified coach, international speaker, and former 49-year-old virgin turned preacher’s wife, Dr. Paula C. Perez, B.S., M.S., Ed.D., and SYMBIS facilitator, teaches single women tools to attract, date, and marry godly men using her 4-STEP™️relationship framework. Her mission stems from her own experience. It is the topic of her memoir, “Delayed Not Denied: How I Became My Best on My Journey to Love and Marriage.” That journey lasted 33 years!
ABC, NBC, CBS, CW, Kingdom TV, and international media have featured Dr. Paula’s expertise. This talk was give
title: 4 essential steps to attract, date, & marry the man of your dreams | Paula C. Perez | TEDxWilmington

author: TEDx Talks
description: In his talk, Professor Jan Miodek shows that speaking beautifully isn't about linguistic showmanship - it's a form of attentiveness toward other people, a way of showing respect through the words we choose. Miodek discusses how language and thought are inseparably intertwined, and how care for correct Polish is, at its core, care for the quality of our relationships with others. As he put it: "Perhaps it's worth learning throughout your whole life (...) how to live." The talk is an invitation to think of language not as a set of rules to follow, but as a tool for building closeness and understanding between people. prof. Jan Miodek an outstanding linguist and a specialist in the field of the Polish language. His works and public appearances contribute to the popularization of knowledge about the Polish language, inspiring and engaging a wide audience. He is always ready to debunk myths and show how fascinating our language can be! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conf
title: The Role of Thought in Language | Jan Miodek | TEDxWSKZ

author: TEDx Talks
description: In her talk, Aneta Korycińska, widely known as "Baba od polskiego", shows that an education system designed for decades around a single, "typical" student has long stopped matching the reality of the classroom. Korycińska discusses neurodiversity - how differently the minds of students with ADHD, autism, or dyslexia function - and why treating these differences as problems to be "fixed," rather than a natural form of variation, harms both students and the teaching process itself. The talk is an invitation to rethink education not as a single path for everyone, but as a system that should adapt to the diversity of minds, rather than the other way around. Polish philologist. Founder of the "Baba od polskiego" brand, which shows that the Polish language does not have to be boring. She combines literature, culture, and humor into engaging educational content. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at
title: How Neurodiversity Is Changing the Way We Think About Education | Aneta Korycińska | TEDxWSKZ

author: TEDx Talks
description: In his talk, Dr. Jędrzej Kowalewski shares the story of Scanway - a company that started as a small Wrocław-based startup and now has its technology operating in orbit. Kowalewski shows that the path from a garage-stage idea to working with the space sector didn't require unlimited resources, but consistency, a willingness to take risks, and the courage to compete with far bigger players on the global market. The talk is both a personal story of entrepreneurship and proof that space - contrary to popular belief - isn't reserved for the few, but increasingly accessible to anyone with an idea and the persistence to pursue it. Founder of Scanway, a company that designs solutions for the space sector - from telescopes to systems used in satellites. He began his journey with student stratospheric experiments, and today he co-creates technologies present in outer space. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Lear
title: Space for Everyone | Jędrzej Kowalewski | TEDxWSKZ

author: TEDx Talks
description: In her talk, Dr. Sylwia Książek shows that how far we go in life depends far more on the decisions we make every day than on the circumstances surrounding us. Książek speaks about courage - not the grand, heroic kind, but the everyday courage it takes to choose the harder, but right, path. The talk is a personal reflection on the idea that where you start never determines where you end up - what happens next is entirely a decision. Certified assessor. She specializes in the area of security and management, combining scientific knowledge with business practice. She supports leaders and organizations in competency development. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Sky Is the Beginning. The Rest Is a Decision. | Sylwia Książek | TEDxWSKZ

author: TEDx Talks
description: In her talk, Martyna Łuszczek argues that climate change isn't just a matter of values and moral choices - it's fundamentally a mathematical problem, one that can be modeled, calculated, and optimized. Łuszczek walks the audience through how data science is reshaping the way we talk about the planet's future: instead of appeals and emotion, the conversation increasingly runs on data, algorithms, and concrete scenarios. The talk is an invitation to see the climate crisis not as an ideological dispute, but as a problem to be solved - spoken in the language of numbers rather than slogans. Young voice of science. At the age of 20, she was already featured on the Forbes 25 under 25 list and among the Top 100 Women in AI. She completed a Data Science Short Program at the prestigious Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). She is the co-creator of Aquacollector - a device designed to collect microplastics from water. Currently, she is studying economics and law. This talk was given at a
title: Climate Is an Optimization Problem | Martyna Łuszczek | TEDxWSKZ

author: TEDx Talks
description: In his talk, Dr. Kamil Stępniak will guide the audience through four pillars underpinning the modern rule of law. He'll begin with dignity - a concept that, however abstract it may sound, is the foundation of every other right we hold, and one that lawyers have long tried to squeeze into a single, precise paragraph. He'll then move on to personal freedom, asking where the line actually falls between what we're allowed to do and what the law forbids - and why that line is far less obvious than it might seem. The third thread will be equality: does the state really treat everyone the same way, and if not, what determines those differences? Finally, Stępniak will turn to the future, discussing the role of lawyers as guardians of this system - and why educating the next generation of lawyers is one of the most important tasks facing universities and the legal community today. PhD in Social Sciences. Legal content creator. Assistant professor at the WSKZ Institute of Law, specializing in c
title: How Much Dignity Fits Into a Person | Kamil Stępniak | TEDxWSKZ

author: TEDx Talks
description: In his talk, Marcin Matych - known more widely as "Dr Nerwica" (Dr. Anxiety) - explores why simply being human is, in itself, a source of unease, and why it can't just be "cured." Matych shows that anxiety, tension, and inner chaos aren't a flaw to be fixed, but an inseparable part of the human condition - something we need to learn to live with rather than fight. The talk is both a personal and clinically grounded account of how understanding our own anxiety can, paradoxically, lead to greater peace of mind. Mental health popularizer. In his work, he shows how to cope with anxiety. Creator of an anxiety disorder therapy method. Author of the guidebooks "How to Live with Anxiety" and "Closeness and Anxiety: How to Build Better Relationships." Known on social media as Dr. Nerwica, he helps thousands of people better understand their emotions and build healthier relationships. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local comm
title: How Being Human Disturbs Our Peace of Mind | Marcin Matych | TEDxWSKZ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Today's universities face a defining question: how can they create value beyond degrees? In this thought-provoking talk, Craig Hobbs explores his world view of Active Campus Ecologies (ACE), a strengths-based framework that reimagines universities and colleges as living innovation ecosystems; where movement, experiential learning, active wellbeing, and community assets are connected through associational life. Using audience participation and the Greater Manchester worker bee and hive as a creative metaphor, he demonstrates how buzzing campus hives can strengthen institutions civic role; foster co-production, reduce inequalities, and pollinate the nectar for active, connected, flourishing, and prosperous "gown and town" communities. Craig Hobbs is a Senior Lecturer in Sport, Public Health and Community at the University of Greater Manchester and an integrated academic - scholarly - practitioner, working across; higher education, sport, health, business, and community disciplines. He f
title: Universities &Colleges Active Campus Ecosystems | Craig Hobbs | TEDxUniversity of Greater Manchester

author: TEDx Talks
description: For centuries, a teacher's job was to be the content provider — pouring knowledge into students trapped in what Kee calls the "information cocoon." Then AI arrived, and teachers everywhere feared obsolescence. Drawing on his own burnout in a Chengdu classroom and his reinvention as an EdTech solopreneur, Kee shares the epiphany that changed everything: the human role isn't to compete with AI as a data engine, but to evolve into a "Learning Architect." Through his R.U.A. method — Recognize, Understand, Apply — he shows how partnering with AI can turn passive consumers into active creators, and makes the case that in an AI age, we should let machines handle the data, and humans handle the humanity. Kee is an independent IELTS trainer and EdTech specialist based in Chengdu. Bridging technology and language learning, he holds a degree in Information Management and Information Systems. Kee began his career at EF Education First, advancing from a Life Club coordinator to an Expert Teacher a
title: Escaping the Information Cocoon with AI | Kee Lee | TEDxWangjiang St

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this moving TEDx talk, Pranav Boxer Grover, model, creator, animal rights advocate, and transgender woman. She takes us through a life lived at the margins and the extraordinary courage it took to claim her own story. From surviving a kidnapping at age nine, to being cast out at eighteen, to battling depression and finding her way back through self-love, her narrative is a raw and radiant testament to what it means to exist boldly in a world that asked her not to.
Pranav explores how identity is shaped, and often crushed by the binaries society imposes from birth, and how the loneliest childhoods can quietly forge the most unbreakable souls. With disarming honesty and warmth, she reveals how a stray dog named Cookie, a six-year-old Labrador named Boxer, and an imagined audience once kept her going, long before a real one ever showed up.
Join us as she unravels what it truly means to belong to yourself, shares hard-won wisdom from a journey spanning survival, transition, and transfo
title: When Nobody Listened, I Learned to Speak | The Second Layer | Pranav Boxer Grover | TEDxSRCASW

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk uses a short story to illustrate the need for perspective, inclusion and accountability in reducing conflict and solving seemingly impossible problems. It contains lessons for each of us in our personal relationships, our organizations and our societies, inviting us to be convenors of conversations that challenge narratives of division and fragmentation.  David specialises in the field of collaboration between individuals, teams and organisations - coaching boards, developing leaders and facilitating change. His work is informed by over 20 years of consulting with organisations undertaking large scale change and integrations where collaboration has been critical to success.

He is the inventor of The Collaboration Game®, a simulation designed to reflect the competing priorities typically found in matrix organisations, helping to develop the skills and behaviours necessary to collaborate effectively.

David is a Programme Director and contributor at both London and Ashridge B
title: Collaborating in the grit of our differences | Dr David Briggs | TEDxHultAshridge

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Air Commodore Romesh Chander Kakar (Retd.), VSM takes us beyond the visible markers of success and into the unseen layers that truly shape human decisions. Drawing from his extensive experience in the Indian Air Force and years of evaluating and mentoring aspirants, he unpacks the subtle forces that operate beneath performance where judgement, responsibility, and character quietly take form.
Through a series of deeply reflective insights, he explores how everyday choices build an internal architecture that reveals itself only under pressure. From navigating responsibility without immediate reward to understanding the source of quiet confidence, from making judicious decisions under uncertainty to balancing conscience with obedience, his talk sheds light on the structures we rarely notice, yet constantly live from.
Air Commodore Kakar invites us to reconsider what truly defines reliability and leadership and not as outward displays, but as inner ali
title: The Hidden Forces Behind Human Decisions | The Second Layer | Romesh Kakar | TEDxSRCASW

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this powerful TEDx talk, psychologist and educator Dr. Itisha Nagar dismantles one of the most damaging questions we ask survivors of intimate partner violence: "Why did she not leave?"
Drawing on research, insight, and her own lived experience in an abusive relationship, she walks us through the stages that trap women in abusive relationships, from love-bombing and isolation to gaslighting, trauma bonding, and the hijacking of the brain's own threat response.
With unflinching honesty, Dr. Nagar challenges the social and cultural systems that silently enable abuse- like patriarchal families, enabling communities, the stigma of divorce, and a society that teaches women that love and control are the same thing. She invites us to stop asking why she didn't leave, and start asking why he abused her and why we let him.
This talk is a call for a more compassionate, survivor-centric world, and a reminder to break the silence on abuse. Dr. Itisha Nagar is a psychologist, educator, feminist
title: Unpacking the Psychology of Abuse | The Second Layer | Dr. Itisha Nagar | TEDxSRCASW

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Un talk sull’autenticità identitaria e sulla forza delle proprie radici che non restano ferme al passato, ma diventano voce e direzione nel mondo.
Francesco Mazzei racconta una storia fatta di grandi sogni, sacrifici silenziosi e cadute prima del successo. Dalla Calabria alle cucine di Londra, il suo percorso dimostra che non si conquista il mondo nonostante le proprie radici, ma portandole con sé come l’unico ingrediente che non si può sostituire. 
Un pitch sul valore dell’autenticità, sulla forza della memoria familiare e sulla capacità di trasformare le proprie origini in una voce riconoscibile ovunque.  Francesco Mazzei è uno chef calabrese riconosciuto tra i principali interpreti della cucina del Sud Italia nel Regno Unito. La sua carriera lo ha portato dalle cucine di Roma a Londra, passando per esperienze in ristoranti stellati Michelin, hotel di lusso e progetti internazionali. 
Nel 2019 ha ricevuto l’Ordine al Merito della Repubblica Italiana per la promozione della gastronom
title: Autenticità identitaria: portare la Calabria nel mondo | Francesco Mazzei | TEDxCosenza

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We picture orphanages as homes for children with no parents — but 4 out of 5 children in orphanages worldwide still have a living parent. Drawing on years of work in China through their organization Hope Station, Rebekah and Margarete reveal that the global orphan crisis is really a family crisis: poverty and disability, not the absence of love, are what push children into institutions. Their message is both a challenge to how we think about "orphans" and a hopeful call to action — that by strengthening struggling families, we can keep children where they belong, and move toward a world without orphanages, one family at a time. I'm currently the COO of Hope Station (Chengdu Together for Children Service Center), where I have served for the past eight years. Since graduating from university, I have been deeply passionate about child welfare and community service.
In 2011, I volunteered as a teacher in Liangshan, Sichuan, and in 2013 began working with children with special needs. I als
title: The Real Reason Children are in Orphanages | Margarete Zhang & Rebekah Kepha | TEDxWangjiang St

author: TEDx Talks
description: Defeat has a way of exposing our deepest fears, but it can also reveal our greatest strengths. In his talk, Abhinav shares how a setback became the turning point that transformed fear into his greatest advantage. Whether you're stepping onto a court, into an exam hall, or towards your biggest ambition, this talk will leave wondering whether fear has been your greatest obstacle, or your greatest opportunity. Abhinav Shukla is a national-level basketball player. Having transitioned from cricket in recent years, he advanced rapidly through district, state, and national competitions to represent India internationally. His experiences on the court inform his perspective on performance under pressure, and in his talk, he reflects on how moments of uncertainty and failure can shape both mindset and growth. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: When Fear Helps You Win! | Abhinav Shukla | TEDxYouth@OIS

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this stirring talk, content creator and influencer Yash Sharma explores the ‘Second layer’ by discussing raw realities of modern creativity. Moving beyond the surface-level glamour of social media, Yash offers a poignant look at the "process" behind the person—the quiet struggles, the constant pivots, and the surging drive required to stay true to one’s vision in a world of noise. He delves into the tumultuous yet rewarding journey of following a dream, arguing that while passion provides the fuel, it is the courage to take risks that opens the door. From the nostalgia of the "Dream College" to the perceptive realization that happiness must be found in the present, Yash shares how resilience and a carefully chosen circle are the ultimate anchors in the chaos. Join us for an illuminating dialogue as Yash breaks down his philosophy that success isn't a final result, but a continuous act of daring. This talk is an invitation to anyone standing at a crossroads: to choose passion over c
title: Forget the Outcome: Let Passion Lead and Risk Follow. | The Second Layer  | Yash Sharma | TEDxSRCASW

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why do some of the smartest students struggle to achieve their goals despite having talent, knowledge, and hard work? The answer often lies not in intelligence, but in clarity.

In this powerful TEDx talk, Dr. Gajendra Purohit explores why academic excellence alone does not guarantee success. Through inspiring stories and practical insights, he explains how having a clear vision, defined goals, and focused action can make the difference between potential and achievement.

Drawing from his experience as an educator and mentor to millions of learners, Dr. Purohit highlights the importance of direction, consistency, and purpose in personal and professional growth. He challenges the common belief that success is driven solely by intelligence and demonstrates how clarity can unlock true potential.

Watch this thought-provoking session to discover why clarity is the ultimate superpower for students, professionals, and lifelong learners.

Event Credits:
Organized by: Mr. Lakhan Varshney
Co-O
title: Why Smart Students Fail: The Power of Clarity | Dr. Gajendra Purohit | TEDxBBAU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Every great composition begins with a single note, and for Christo Xavier, that note was a dream he nurtured from the tenth grade. In this inspiring talk, he traces his journey from teaching himself music production through online tutorials and creating music on a modest 2 GB computer to becoming one of the most distinctive voices in Malayalam cinema. Reflecting on his early aspirations, his experience assisting Sushin Shyam and his work on films including June, Kappela, Madanolsavam, Journey of Love 18+ and Bramayugam, Christo reveals the creative process behind crafting memorable background scores. Through stories of experimenting with folk instruments, recording ambient sounds in remote villages and transforming everyday objects into haunting sonic textures, he demonstrates that innovation is born not from abundance, but from curiosity, resourcefulness and an unwavering commitment to one's craft.

Christo Xavier is an Indian music composer, producer and sound designer known for his
title: Every Dream Begins with a Note  | Christo Xavier | TEDxMEC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Language is more than a means of communication - it has the power to shape identity. In this insightful talk, Sreekanth K G explores the profound relationship between language, thought and self-expression, illustrating how learning a new language can lead to the discovery of a new version of oneself. Reflecting on his own transformation from an underconfident speaker to a confident communicator, he explains how changes in language influence not only the way we think and speak, but also our body language, presence and personality. Reflecting on concepts such as language persona and vocal setting, he examines how speech production, expression and mindset evolve together, revealing the profound connection between language and identity. His talk challenges us to see language not merely as a skill to be acquired, but as a catalyst for personal growth and transformation.

Sreekanth K G is a leading digital educator and English pronunciation coach, best known as the creator of Voice of Sreek
title: The Identity You Speak Into Existence | Sreekanth KG | TEDxMEC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What began with a simple cup of chai and a bun grew into a journey driven by purpose, passion and perseverance. In this inspiring talk, the Chai Couple shares how their time working in restaurants during their master's studies sparked a shared love for cooking and encouraged them to pursue an unconventional path. From borrowing a kettle from their grandmother to opening a modest café where they could personally witness every customer's reaction, they embraced the power of simplicity and authenticity. Their journey challenges the notion that success is defined by scale, proving instead that quality, consistency and genuine human connection leave the greatest impact. Reflecting on their evolution, they encourage young dreamers to pursue what they truly love, reminding us that every meaningful venture begins with the courage to take the first step.

The talk is both a provocation and an invitation to rethink what we're actually teaching the next generation - and why the ability to think mathematically may matter more than ever.
